units.text: RFC 9110 (June 2022, STD 97) defines safe methods as GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, and TRACE per Section 9.2.1. These safe methods are explicitly listed as idempotent in Section 9.2.2, which states that PUT, DELETE, and all safe request methods are idempotent. The complete idempotent set is GET, HEAD, OPTIONS

judgement.reason: Passages support the safe methods and that safe methods plus PUT/DELETE are idempotent, but they state the complete idempotent set is GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, TRACE, PUT, and DELETE, contradicting the statement's truncated set.

units.text: POST and PATCH are not idempotent, and CONNECT is not idempotent, as clearly stated in the RFC classifications. The claim 'every safe HTTP request method is idempotent' is therefore true because all safe methods (GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, TRACE) are confirmed idempotent.

judgement.reason: The passages support that POST and PATCH are not idempotent and that GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, and TRACE are idempotent, but they do not mention CONNECT at all, so the statement about CONNECT is missing.

units.text: The June 2022 standard used worldwide (RFC 9110, STD 97) provides the authoritative classification. Evidence from restguide.info citations with IETF origin confirms the standard's scope and method properties match the claim's timeframe and population requirements.
